messages.text: I have a non-heated garage that can go down to -20C on occasion.  Can a miner survive those temperatures?

Running, yes. A miner makes its own heat, so -20C ambient is not the problem. The risk is the cold start and the downtime: a unit that sits at -20C and then powers up, or warms up after a stop, gets condensation on the board. Keep it in a closed box or cabinet so it keeps its own warm pocket, and avoid frequent on/off cycles.

Are you mining mainly for the heat, or is the garage just the only space you have?
Neither.  Just looking at options.
Read the magic miner 40t page
Read the bsb b30 page

Fair enough. Two we'd point you at for a cold garage, both quiet and self-contained with the PSU built in.

Harlo B30, 30 TH/s at about 360 to 450W, $899, ships October 30, 2026. Magic Miner 40T, 40 TH/s at about 650W, $799, ships November 14, 2026. The 40T is the better value per terahash and runs warmer, which helps in an unheated space.

What's your rough budget, and roughly what do you pay per kWh?
What currency are we talking about?

USD. Every price on the site is in US dollars.

Tax depends on where you are. US and Canada: no import VAT or duty, sales tax added at checkout where it applies. UK and most of the EU: the price excludes VAT, so 21% import VAT plus any duty is charged on delivery by the carrier, we don't collect it at checkout. Shipping is separate and calculated from your address at checkout.

Where would it be shipping to?
Sherwood P., AB, Canada
Ran the power-cost calculator

Good, Canada means no import VAT or duty, just sales tax at checkout where it applies and shipping from your address.

For an Alberta garage I'd take the Magic Miner 40T. More hashrate, cheaper, and the extra heat it throws is useful rather than a problem in that space. $799, ships November 14, 2026. The B30 is the pick if you want the lower draw at 360 to 450W.

Want me to put one in a cart so you can see shipping to (address hidden)?
Are mining pools still a thing, or am I on my own for finding a winner?

Pools are very much still a thing, and you choose. Point the miner at a pool and you get small, steady payouts in proportion to your hashrate. Point it at a solo pool or your own node and you get nothing until you hit a block, then the whole reward.

At 40 TH/s the solo odds are long, so most people run a pool and treat solo as the lottery ticket. Either way it's a setting in the dashboard, switchable any time.

Which way are you leaning?
Pools me would think.  Are any of your miner also connected to the lightning network?

The miner itself doesn't run a Lightning node. It hashes and points at a pool, that's it.

Lightning comes in on the payout side: several pools will pay you to a Lightning address, which gets you small payouts without waiting to clear a minimum on-chain. That's a choice you make at the pool, not in the miner, so any unit we sell can do it.

Is there a specific pool or wallet you had in mind? I can check what the firmware needs for it.
Which unit is your quietest if I choose to put one in a bedroom?
Read the nexus s1 10th s page
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page

The Hammer Miner Thor P2 is our quietest, about 40 dB, 10 TH/s at roughly 166W. $369, ships October 3, 2026.

Honest limit: 40 dB is a soft fan hum, fine in a room you work in, but most people notice it when trying to sleep. The B30 and Magic Miner are both around 50 dB, which is too much for a bedroom in my view.

If the bedroom is the plan, the Thor P2 is the one. Want the link?
Does the hammer miner thor P2 mine just btc, or Doge and LTC as well?

Bitcoin only. The T. P2 is a SHA-256 ASIC, and Doge and Litecoin run on Scrypt, which is different hardware entirely.

For Scrypt we list the Hammer DC06 at 330 MH/s, which merge-mines LTC and DOGE. Straight answer though: it's oversold and past its ship window, so I can't give you a date on it right now. I wouldn't have you waiting on it.

Is Scrypt something you actually want, or was that curiosity?
I thought is makes sense to work multiple chains for the same power cost.

You're right, within one algorithm. A Scrypt miner gets LTC and DOGE from the same work, so the second chain is genuinely free power-wise. Same on SHA-256, where some pools merge-mine smaller coins alongside Bitcoin.

What no machine does is both algorithms. The chips are built for one or the other, so it's a choice between a BTC box and a Scrypt box, not a combined one.

Given the DC06 has no date, my call is the BTC side for now.
Send me a link for Thor P2.  I'll go have a looksie.

Here you go: https://heliumdeploy.com/products/hammer-miner-thor-p2

$369, 10 TH/s at about 166W, roughly 40 dB, ships October 3, 2026. Plug is matched to your Canadian address, and no import VAT or duty into Canada.

Shout if you want me to build a cart so you can see shipping to (address hidden), or if you'd rather weigh it against the Magic Miner for the garage.
Are people still mining helium, or is that mostly dead now?

Alive, but changed. The old IoT side is a trickle now, nowhere near the 2021 numbers, so I wouldn't buy an IoT hotspot expecting income.

The active side is Helium Mobile, the 5G coverage hotspots, and earnings there depend heavily on whether there's real demand where you live. We do stock those. I'd want to confirm whether Alberta is in the covered area before I let you buy one, so let me check that rather than guess.

Is Helium something you're seriously considering, or just curious?

I have a couple Helium miner and I'm wondering why.
Please check on my area for 5G.

I can't confirm Helium Mobile coverage for (address hidden) from here, and I won't guess on something that decides whether a hotspot earns anything.

I've put it to Georges to check Alberta coverage properly. The team is offline right now and picks this up tomorrow at 10am ET, and the answer comes to your email, so no need to wait here.

What email should it go to?
Handed to the team · Cannot verify Helium Mobile coverage for Alberta from available tools; will not
That's with Georges now. Drop me the email address and he'll send the Alberta coverage answer there tomorrow.
(email hidden)

Got it, (email hidden) is on the note to Georges. He'll come back on the Alberta coverage tomorrow.

Meanwhile the Thor P2 link is there whenever you want a closer look. If the garage ends up being the spot rather than the bedroom, say the word and I'll line it up against the Magic Miner 40T for you.
Which would be better for both locations.  I would probably leave it inside for the winter and move it outside for the summer.

Thor P2, for that pattern. It's the quietest at about 40 dB so it can live indoors in winter, it's small and light to carry out in summer, and at 166W it won't heat a room you don't want heated.

One caution: none of our miners are weatherproof. "Outside" has to mean the garage or a covered shelter, not open air, and watch for dust and humidity swings when you move it.

Want me to build the cart?
No.  Should I unplug my helium miners in exchange for a btc miner?

They're not really competing. A Helium hotspot draws about five watts, so leaving them plugged in costs you almost nothing even if they earn almost nothing. I wouldn't pull them to fund a BTC miner.

The honest question is whether you want to spend the $369 or $799 at all, and what you pay per kWh in Alberta. A BTC miner at retail power is mostly about stacking sats steadily, not clearing a profit.

What's your rate per kWh?
$0.09 CAD in winter $0.30 CAD in summer.  I have solar panels on the house.

That's a nice setup, and it flips the usual logic. Winter at 9 cents, in a garage where the heat isn't wasted, is when a bigger unit makes sense.

Rough monthly power: Thor P2 at 166W is about 120 kWh, so $11 in winter, $36 in summer. Magic Miner 40T at 650W is about 470 kWh, $42 winter, $140 summer. Harlo B30 at 450W sits between.

Solar helps most in summer daylight, but a miner runs 24/7, so nights still come off the grid at 30 cents.

My call: Thor P2 if you want it painless year round, Magic Miner if you'll run it hard in winter and throttle or idle it in summer.
How much can the P2 earn / month at $80k/btc if I am in a pool?
Ran the power-cost calculator · 9¢/kWh

Rough numbers, and treat them as today's estimate since difficulty and price move.

At 10 TH/s against a network around 1,000 EH/s, you're looking at roughly 400 to 500 sats a day, call it 13,000 sats a month, about $10 to $11 USD at $80k BTC, less a 1 to 2 percent pool fee.

Against power of about $11 CAD winter and $36 CAD summer, that's roughly break-even in winter and a loss in summer at 30 cents.

So it's a sat-stacking and heat machine, not an income one. Does that change your thinking?
Well, it doesn't help.  However, perhaps the heat output in the winter helps the math.  And maybe I unplug it during the warm months.

That's the right read, with one check: the heat only pays you back if you'd otherwise be heating with electricity. If the house runs on a gas furnace, electric heat is the more expensive kind, so the offset is partial.

And if winter-only is the plan, the bigger unit is the better buy. At 650W the Magic Miner 40T gives you four times the hashrate and real heat for the room, and sitting idle all summer costs nothing.

What heats the house, gas or electric?
Gas and electric.

Then put it where the electric heat runs. Anywhere you'd otherwise use a baseboard or space heater, the miner replaces that heat watt for watt, so at 9 cents the power is doing a job you were paying for anyway and the sats come free.

On that basis the Magic Miner 40T is the one, $799, 40 TH/s, ships November 14, 2026. Four times the Thor P2's hashrate for the same heat you were buying.

Gas-heated rooms, the maths is weaker. Which rooms run electric?
So much to consider.  I'm running out of battery power on my laptop, so I'll have to come back to this later.
Used the chat-interview skill

No rush, the links will keep. Georges' Alberta coverage answer lands in your inbox tomorrow.

Before you go, one thing: what's making it hard to pick between the Thor P2 and the 40T?
I have to decide how I will use the unit.  The P2 seems the most versatile.  It looks like I really need the price of BTC to increase to make this worthwhile.

That's a fair reading, and I won't talk you out of it. At retail power the sats you stack are worth roughly what the electricity costs today, so the upside is mostly in where BTC goes, plus the heat you'd have paid for anyway.

The P2 is the versatile pick, you're right there.

One more, then I'll let your battery rest: is it the money side holding you back, or the hassle of running it?
Money.

Understood, and that's an honest reason not to rush. Thanks for talking it through, it helps us.

Everything we covered comes to your email as a copy once this chat closes, along with Georges' coverage answer tomorrow. Come back any time and we'll pick it up from here.
Thanks.
Any time. Good luck with the garage plan, and go charge that laptop.
